discovery: Public WordPress media API; these PDFs were not linked in the seven vessel detail-page link sets.
scope: Historical company-published ship-particulars sheets, not independently authenticated current vessel certificates.
method: All seven PDFs downloaded with HTTP 200, text extracted with pypdf and complete one-page Poppler renderings visually inspected. Visible technical fields were compared with the direct HTML tables. Stray hidden text was excluded from the interpreted values.

companyFooterAsPublished.warning: Do not assign this company's registration or historical particulars to Moe Navigation without confirming the legal relationship.

commonFindings: Every container-vessel sheet visibly states five reefer plugs; every matching HTML detail states three. Both values must remain attributed to their source until the current configuration is confirmed.

Outside the differences listed for each sheet, the visible vessel identity, dimensions, tonnage, machinery, fuel-consumption values and tank capacities agree with fleet-data.json after line-break and whitespace normalization.

The PDFs have no future validity claim or certificate number for the vessel particulars. Their printed update dates are historical source version dates, not a guarantee that the equipment remains unchanged.
No MMSI or LBP is present for MOE LINE 1/RANONG MOE in either the HTML or its particulars sheet.

documents.note: The vessel name and photograph support a historical MOE LINE 1 identity for this IMO; the documents do not establish a legal rename or why the nominal capacity changed.

documents.extractionNote: The text layer repeats a machinery block that is not a second visible set of equipment; do not count duplicated extraction as extra engines.
A stray BUILT 2008 string appears in the text layer but is not the rendered general-details value. The visible sheet and HTML both show 2011, China.
